decisions.reason: The 1.27 mm pitch decision concerns the integrated-board ESP32 breakout, not the distinct main-board breakout. The source does not change the main-board breakout pitch or its existing full-pin-access requirements.
Changing the integrated ESP32 breakout pitch does not alter the single-board architecture, functional consolidation, or functionality-preservation requirements.
The source specifies a breakout-header pitch but does not change the integrated board's cost goal, component-tier preference, connector-reduction strategy, or sourcing exception.
The ESP32 breakout pitch has no entailed effect on charging behavior, required power rails, battery efficiency, or the AXP2101 power-management choice.
A 1.27 mm ESP32 pin-header pitch remains compatible with the existing through-hole connector-assembly requirement and does not change its assembly type or coverage.
The breakout-header pitch does not affect the required current-measurement capability or the conditional omission of a separate INA device.
The ESP32 breakout pitch does not modify the display-backlight connector, switching circuit, supply options, PWM control, or related component values.
The source does not change the separate I2C JST light-sensor port or any of its connector attributes.
The source concerns the integrated-board ESP32 breakout and does not alter the connector inventory or connector pitches recorded for the separate main board.
The 1.27 mm integrated ESP32 pin-header pitch does not change any sensor-board input or output connector topology, including the independently specified 1.25 mm signal connector.
The integrated ESP32 breakout pitch has no necessary effect on the separate power-board AXP2101 topology, net labeling, or thermal-pad requirement.
The integrated-board ESP32 breakout pitch is unrelated to the separate LED board's LED count, model, package, and array requirements.
